subject: Next steps: VPC onramp & connectivity checklist for HealthVerse
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@healthverse.com>, HealthVerse IT <it@healthverse.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: VPC onramp & connectivity checklist for HealthVerse

Priya / team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap (from our discussion)
- Goal: Host Redwood inference with private connectivity for PHI-handling inference requests from HealthVerse product.
- Priority items: VPC private connectivity (no public egress), client-auth (mTLS preferred), IP allowlist for fallback services, embedding storage accessibility, and reranker placement (hosted vs local).

Open questions we promised to follow up on
1) Preferred connectivity model: AWS PrivateLink (Private VPC endpoint) vs Transit VPC. Do you need cross-account VPC peering or PrivateLink service?
2) mTLS termination: do you require Redwood to present a customer-managed cert/HSM integration, or is mutual TLS with provided client certs sufficient?
3) Egress/egress restrictions: Can Redwood make outbound requests to S3 or do you need all storage traffic over the private link?
4) DNS: Will HealthVerse provide an internal DNS entry for the Redwood endpoint, or do you want us to inject an internal CNAME?
5) Embeddings store: do you prefer we write vectors to your S3 (via VPC endpoint) or recommend a managed vector DB inside your VPC?

Proposed next steps
- HealthVerse: share the connectivity requirements worksheet (attach), list of IP ranges and desired DNS name, and a short diagram of existing network boundaries.
- Redwood: Connor and Monica will produce a technical onramp checklist (VPC endpoint types, cert options, SDK config snippets) within 24 business hours.
- We’ll schedule a 30-min architecture review with your infra team next week to align on any guardrails.

Attachments: initial-call-notes.pdf, healthverse_connectivity_request.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the internal checklist and suggested timeline.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0128

From: Priya Shah <priya@healthverse.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthVerse IT <it@healthverse.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: VPC onramp & connectivity checklist for HealthVerse

Ben — thanks for the write-up and the clear next steps. A few answers and clarifications from our side:

Answers / constraints
- Connectivity model: We prefer PrivateLink for SaaS integrations where possible. Cross-account peering is allowed but introduces longer approval timelines. PrivateLink would be preferred if Redwood supports it.
- mTLS: Security requires mutual TLS. Our security team expects client cert validation and prefers that Redwood can accept customer-provided client certs; if you support integration with our CA or HSM for cert verification, that would be ideal.
- Egress: We have a strict no-internet-egress policy for workloads that touch PHI. Any storage calls (examples: to S3) must be reachable via private connectivity (VPC endpoint) or happen inside our VPC.
- DNS: We would like to map an internal DNS name (redwood.healthverse.internal) to the PrivateLink endpoint; HealthVerse IT will manage the internal DNS zone.
- Embeddings: Preference is for vectors to remain within our environment. Option A: Redwood can write embeddings to a private S3 bucket via a VPC endpoint. Option B: we host a Milvus/managed vector DB in our VPC and give Redwood write access. Security prefers Option B but will accept Option A with tightening on access controls.

Deliverables from HealthVerse this week
- Connectivity worksheet (attached)
- Short network diagram and current IP space
- Security runbook excerpt describing mTLS expectations

We will be available for a technical review on Thursday morning (PDT). Please loop in anyone on your infra/SE team who will own the implementation.

Thanks,
Priya
Director, Platform Security | HealthVerse
priya@healthverse.com

[Attachment: healthverse_connectivity_request.xlsx (xlsx)]

On Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben / Monica — thanks for looping us in. Below is a concise technical onramp checklist and a proposed implementation approach. I’ve kept it actionable so we can hand this to HV during the architecture review.
>
> Redwood technical onramp checklist (private connectivity + auth)
> 1) Connectivity & endpoint
>    - Support PrivateLink (AWS NLB-backed PrivateLink service) — Redwood will provision a PrivateLink endpoint service in our account and publish the service name. HV must create an Interface VPC Endpoint in their VPC and accept the VPC endpoint attachment.
>    - Alternate: Cross-account VPC peering for customers that cannot use PrivateLink; note longer approvals and routing/NAT considerations.
>
> 2) DNS & internal name mapping
>    - HV provides an internal DNS name (e.g., redwood.healthverse.internal).
>    - Redwood will publish the PrivateLink DNS name; HV's DNS team will create an internal CNAME pointing to the PrivateLink-managed endpoint.
>
> 3) mTLS and certs
>    - Option A (preferred for HV): HV provides a client cert signed by their CA. Redwood will validate client certs at the edge (mTLS) and map cert subject to HV tenant.
>    - Option B (if customer cannot share certs): short-lived API keys + IP allowlist as a fallback (less preferred for PHI workloads).
>    - For HSM integration: we support validating cert chains against a customer CA bundle; HSM-managed keys on HV side are fine. Redwood does not store customer private keys.
>
> 4) Egress & storage
>    - To meet no-internet-egress: Embeddings writes should go to a customer-managed S3 bucket accessible via a VPC gateway/private endpoint. Redwood can write via PrivateLink or assume a cross-account role scoped to a limited prefix.
>    - If HV hosts a vector DB (Milvus/Weaviate), Redwood will provide a secure write API over the PrivateLink path; recommend minimal network ACLs and security group rules.
>
> 5) SDK/auth implications
>    - SDKs: support for mTLS client certificates in our HTTP client, and a configuration flag to point to the internal DNS name. Example snippets (will provide in doc).
>    - Tool calling / structured output: webhooks and tool callbacks must be reachable over the private path. Recommend a webhook relay that accepts requests from Redwood and posts internally over the PrivateLink.
>
> 6) Embeddings & reranker placement
>    - Recommendation: keep embedding storage inside HV VPC. For reranking, two options: run the reranker hosted by Redwood but called via a private route (requires tight SLOs), or run the reranker inside HV VPC (lower latency and full data control).
>
> 7) Rollout plan & fallbacks
>    - Phase 1: Proof-of-concept using non-PHI test corpus with PrivateLink and test cert.
>    - Phase 2: Canary with production traffic to a dedicated model variant; monitor latency and error rates in Console.
>    - Fallback: If PrivateLink is unavailable, route to confined-hosted variant and enforce stricter prompt/data redaction.
>
> Deliverables from Redwood
> - PrivateLink service name and onboarding doc.
> - SDK snippets for mTLS + internal DNS config.
> - Network diagram and minimal security group / NACL templates.
> - Embedding write patterns (S3 cross-account role example) and optional vector DB API.
> - Onramp checklist doc (attached).
>
> Attachments: redwood_private_onramp_checklist.docx
>
> Happy to review this with their infra team on Thursday morning. Connor
